title: Reading Arabic Grammar in Arabic: الجُمْلَة الاسْمِيَّة and الفِعْلِيَّة, أَقْسَام الكَلِمَة, and لَمَّا
summary: A landmark session: the lesson explains Arabic grammar in Arabic, and the class can follow it. الجُمْلَة الاسْمِيَّة is defined as the sentence whose first word is a noun, with its مُبْتَدَأ and خَبَر both مَرْفُوع; الجُمْلَة الفِعْلِيَّة begins with a verb, and the noun following takes the name فَاعِل. The three أَقْسَام الكَلِمَة are named, with حَرْف as the category holding everything that is neither noun nor verb, and the new particle لَمَّا turns out to be لَمْ with the added sense of not yet.
key_points: الجُمْلَة الاسْمِيَّة (al-jumlah al-ismiyyah) is the sentence whose first word is an اسْم: السَّيَّارَةُ جَمِيلَةٌ، حَامِدٌ مَرِيضٌ. Its first word is the مُبْتَدَأ and the second the خَبَر, and both are مَرْفُوع.

الجُمْلَة الفِعْلِيَّة (al-jumlah al-fiʿliyyah) begins with a فِعْل: دَخَلَ الْمُدَرِّسُ، قَالَ الْمُدِيرُ، كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ. The اسْم coming after the verb is called the فَاعِل, and it too is مَرْفُوع.
مَرْفُوع simply means carrying a ḍamma — the formal term for what the class had been told plainly all along.
أَقْسَام الْكَلِمَة (aqsām al-kalimah : the categories of the word) are three: الاسْم، الفِعْل، الحَرْف. قِسْم means a category, as in Urdu, with the plural أَقْسَام.

الحَرْف is the catch-all category for whatever is neither noun nor verb. It need not be a single letter — لَمْ، لَنْ، مَا are all حُرُوف — and it does not necessarily affect the word after it, though it often does.
The سِين counts as a حَرْف in its own right: not any sīn, but specifically the one prefixed to a مُضَارِع verb to make it future, which is why the lesson had to specify كَمَا فِي سَأَذْهَبُ.
لَمَّا behaves like لَمْ — it takes a مُضَارِع verb, puts it in jazm, and gives past meaning — but it adds the sense of not yet: لَمَّا أَفْهَمْ means I have not understood yet.
The person is built into the verb, so لَمْ أَفْهَمْ already means I did not understand; the أَنَا is optional emphasis rather than a requirement.
سَأَلَ takes the person asked as its direct object, but what is asked about takes عَنْ: سَأَلْتُ الْمُدَرِّسَ عَنِ الْقُرْآنِ, I asked the teacher about the Qur'ān.
The سِين removes ambiguity about time: نَبْدَأُ could mean we begin now or we will begin, while سَنَبْدَأُ can only be the future.

ذُو shifts shape by case — ذُو with a ḍamma, ذَا with a fatḥa, ذِي with a kasra — which is why it is ذُو الْجَلَالِ as a صِفَة of وَجْهُ, ذِي الْجَلَالِ as a صِفَة of رَبِّكَ, and يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ in supplication.
After يَا, a single noun takes a ḍamma but a مُضَاف takes a fatḥa — يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، يَا رَبَّنَا، يَا أُسْتَاذَنَا.
قَبْلَ makes the following word a مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ in the genitive, so the dual appears as يَوْمَيْنِ rather than يَوْمَانِ.
مَهْلًا means take it easy or calm down, from the root behind تَمَهَّلْ on Saudi road signs meaning slow down. It is unrelated to مَهْلَك, from هَلَكَ, destruction.
Vocabulary: مَرَّة أُخْرَى (again, another time), نَحْوُ used to mean such as or for example, حِصَّة (a class period), بَدَأَ (to begin), and اِسْتَرِحْ قَلِيلًا (rest a little).
questions: [00:01:00] Q: What are the special properties of لَمْ? — A: It makes the following verb sākin, drops the نُون where the verb has one, and gives past meaning despite attaching to a مُضَارِع verb.
[00:05:00] Q: Does اسْم here mean name? — A: No. In this context اسْم means noun — one of the three categories of word, alongside فِعْل and حَرْف.
[00:09:00] Q: What does مَرْفُوع mean? — A: In Arabic grammar it simply means that the word carries a ḍamma — the formal term for what had been described plainly until now.
[00:13:00] Q: Why is أَنَا written in لَمْ أَفْهَمْ if the verb already means I did not understand? — A: It is not necessary. أَفْهَمُ already carries the first person; the pronoun is optional.
[00:14:00] Q: What exactly does لَمَّا add? — A: The sense of yet. لَمْ أَفْهَمْ is I did not understand; لَمَّا أَفْهَمْ is I have not understood yet.

[00:25:00] Q: How can سِين be a حَرْف — isn't it just a letter? — A: حَرْف is the category for whatever is neither noun nor verb, and the one meant is specifically the سِين prefixed to a verb for the future, which is why the lesson says كَمَا فِي سَأَذْهَبُ.
[00:26:00] Q: Doesn't a حَرْف have to affect the word after it? — A: Usually it does, but not always; that is not what defines the category.
[00:21:00] Q: Why is it يَوْمَيْنِ and not يَوْمَانِ? — A: Because قَبْلَ makes the following word a مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ with a kasra, and the dual shows that as ـَيْنِ.
[00:30:00] Q: Why add the سِين if نَبْدَأُ can already mean the future? — A: To remove ambiguity. Without it, some would understand we begin now and others we will begin next time.
[00:34:11] Q: Is مَهْلًا related to مَهْلَك, destruction? — A: No, they are separate words. مَهْلًا is from the root meaning to go gently; مَهْلَك comes from هَلَكَ.

[00:36:00] Q: Why is it ذُو in one āyah and ذِي in another? — A: Because it matches the case of what it describes: ذُو الْجَلَالِ follows وَجْهُ, which is مَرْفُوع, while ذِي الْجَلَالِ follows رَبِّكَ, which is in the genitive.

quiz.q: What makes a sentence a جُمْلَة اسْمِيَّة?
options: Its first word is a noun
It has no verb at all
quiz.a: The lesson's own definition: الْجُمْلَةُ الَّتِي أَوَّلُهَا اسْمٌ — the sentence whose beginning is a noun.

quiz.q: In a جُمْلَة اسْمِيَّة, what are the first and second parts called?
quiz.a: The مُبْتَدَأ is the subject and the خَبَر the information given about it, and both are مَرْفُوع.

quiz.q: What is the noun following the verb in a جُمْلَة فِعْلِيَّة called?
quiz.a: دَخَلَ الْمُدَرِّسُ — الْمُدَرِّس is the فَاعِل, and it is مَرْفُوع.
The teacher had avoided the term until now, describing it plainly as taking a ḍamma.

quiz.q: What are the three أَقْسَام الْكَلِمَة?
quiz.a: قِسْم means a category, and the three categories of word are noun, verb and particle.

quiz.q: Which statement about الحَرْف is correct?
options: It is always a single letter
It is the category for what is neither noun nor verb, and may be more than one letter
It must always affect the following word
It is a type of noun
quiz.a: لَمْ، لَنْ، مَا are all حُرُوف, and a حَرْف does not necessarily affect what follows it.

quiz.q: What does لَمَّا add to the meaning of لَمْ?
quiz.a: لَمَّا أَفْهَمْ is I have not understood yet, as against لَمْ أَفْهَمْ, I did not understand.

quiz.q: How do you say I asked the teacher about the Qur'ān?
quiz.a: The person asked is the direct object; the subject matter takes عَنْ.

quiz.q: Why is it يَا أُسْتَاذَنَا with a fatḥa?
options: Because it is a مُضَاف after يَا
quiz.a: A single noun after يَا takes a ḍamma, but a مُضَاف takes a fatḥa — as in يَا رَبَّنَا and يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ.
The same root as تَمَهَّلْ on road signs meaning slow down — unrelated to مَهْلَك from هَلَكَ.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَتِ الْأَعْرَابُ آمَنَّا ۖ قُل لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَلَٰكِن قُولُوا أَسْلَمْنَا وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ الْإِيمَانُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ
quran_examples.transliteration: qālati al-aʿrābu āmannā, qul lam tuʾminū wa-lākin qūlū aslamnā wa-lammā yadkhuli al-īmānu fī qulūbikum
quran_examples.translation: The bedouins say: We have believed. Say: You have not believed; but say: We have submitted — for faith has not yet entered your hearts.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example, and it carries both particles side by side: لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا with the نُون dropped, and لَمَّا يَدْخُلْ adding the sense of not yet. He also drew out its meaning, that īmān is a higher level than merely having accepted Islam.

quran_examples.arabic: وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-yabqā wajhu rabbika dhū al-jalāli wa-l-ikrām
quran_examples.translation: And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour.
quran_examples.note: ذُو with a ḍamma here, because it describes وَجْهُ, which is مَرْفُوع; it also uses بَقِيَ، يَبْقَى from an earlier lesson.

quran_examples.arabic: تَبَارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
quran_examples.transliteration: tabāraka smu rabbika dhī al-jalāli wa-l-ikrām
quran_examples.translation: Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour.
quran_examples.note: The same phrase with ذِي instead, because here it describes رَبِّكَ, which carries a kasra — the teacher's pair for showing how ذُو shifts with case.

quran_examples.arabic: وَذَرْنِي وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-dharnī wa-l-mukadhdhibīna ulī al-niʿmati wa-mahhilhum qalīlā
quran_examples.translation: And leave Me with the deniers, those of ease, and allow them a little respite.
quran_examples.note: A student identified the sūrah when مَهْلًا came up: وَمَهِّلْهُمْ is from the same root, meaning to give time — and it sits on the فَعَّلَ pattern as an imperative.
